title: The Nandi: Their Language and Folk-Lore
author: A. C. Hollis
notes: Complete with index; OCR readable (some noise on plates). Book is mixed: Part I ethnography (social organisation, customs, religion; roughly a third of the book, well above 30k words), Part II grammar, Part III folk-lore. Flag: not purely ethnographic.

title: The Bontoc Igorot
author: Albert Ernest Jenks
notes: Project Gutenberg #3308; complete (letter of transmittal to final language notes, Gutenberg end marker). IA Google scan also complete: https://archive.org/download/bontocigorot00jenkgoog/bontocigorot00jenkgoog_djvu.txt. Ethnological Survey Publications vol. 1 (Manila). Distinct from the excluded Ifugao.

title: The Ainu and Their Folk-Lore
author: John Batchelor
notes: Complete, 39 chapters plus index; OCR readable. Covers customs, social life and religion as well as folk-lore.

title: The Natives of Mailu: Preliminary Results of the Robert Mond Research Work in British New Guinea (Transactions of the Royal Society of South Australia 39: 494-706)
author: Bronislaw Malinowski
notes: Digital Library of India scan of the whole journal volume (~340k words). The monograph runs from the heading 'The Natives of Mailu' (about character 1,145,600) to the start of S. A. White's 'Scientific Notes on an Expedition' (about character 1,668,400): ~90k words, complete with plate list. OCR readable. Not the excluded Trobriands.

author: A. C. Haddon (ed.), with W. H. R. Rivers, C. G. Seligmann, A. Wilkin and others

title: The Pima Indians (26th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, accompanying paper)
author: Frank Russell
notes: Google scan of the separately bound paper; runs through the final plates; no index in this scan (the report index is in the full volume). OCR readable. Distinct from the excluded Hopi and Tarahumara.

title: Tsimshian Mythology (31st Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology)
author: Franz Boas (texts recorded by Henry W. Tate)
notes: Complete annual report volume through index (~554k tokens); OCR readable apart from cover noise. Flag: weak fit, mainly myths and comparative study; includes Boas's long 'Description of the Tsimshian, based on their mythology' (social organisation, customs, religion). No dedicated pre-1929 Tsimshian ethnography found online.

title: Life and Culture of the Hupa (University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 1(1))
author: Pliny Earle Goddard
notes: Google scan; complete (88 pp. plus plates and series list); OCR readable. Flag: short, close to the 30k-word floor (~35k words of text after boilerplate).

title: The Zuñi Indians: Their Mythology, Esoteric Fraternities, and Ceremonies (23rd Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology)
author: Matilda Coxe Stevenson
notes: IA date 1905 (report for 1901-02, printed 1904). Complete volume through index; OCR readable. Strong on religion and ceremonies; also covers social customs, sociology and arts.

title: Indian Tribes of the Lower Mississippi Valley and Adjacent Coast of the Gulf of Mexico (BAE Bulletin 43)
author: John R. Swanton
notes: Google scan; complete with index; OCR readable. Flag: covers several tribes and is reconstructed mainly from 18th-century French sources; the Natchez account is the core and largest part (well over 30k words).
